- When sentiment is consistently high (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast peaks by 15–30%.
- When sentiment is low (≤0.33) and prices are trending upward, model underestimates; increase forecast by 10–25% to capture momentum.
- After a sharp price spike (true outcome > 15), model often overshoots in next 3–5 days; apply a “cool-down” correction: subtract 20–40% from forecasted values.
- If sentiment history shows alternating high-low cycles, model exhibits mean reversion bias; adjust forecast to align with recent sentiment trend direction.
- For 30-day horizon, model frequently overpredicts in early days (1–7) when sentiment is volatile; dampen early forecast values by 10–20%.
- When sentiment is flat (0.33–0.67) and history shows no clear trend, model tends to underperform; use median of recent 5-day history as baseline for correction.
